=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:12, 187, 190 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The issue-mode cleanup trigger is described in Step 0 even though it requires the `Source issue:` identifier from the plan read in Step 1, and no operational instruction ensures it runs after that read.
  WHY: A session may attempt cleanup before the identifier is available or defer it without returning to run it, leaving the stopped stage session unarchived after `/reclarify`.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md):187 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The cleanup header says every stage session runs cleanup in Step 0, although the issue-mode resume-without-block path explicitly defers cleanup until Step 1 has read the plan.
  WHY: This is documentation imprecision rather than a runtime defect because the deferral bullet explicitly gives the later timing.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "When an issue-mode `/implement-plan-claude` project stops (`Status: BLOCKED`), the stage session that stopped stays open after a human answers on the issue and comments `/reclarify`. It then has to be archived by hand." The fix's contract is that the cleanup actually fires on `/reclarify` resume, after Step 1 reads the plan and the `Source issue:` identifier is available.
  expected_change_site: `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` and `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: No diff hunk places the issue-mode cleanup trigger inside Step 1 or appends an operational hook at the end of Step 1; the new Step 0 child bullet at line 12 and the line-190 "Issue mode: stopped stage sessions." bullet describe the cleanup but provide no runtime mechanism that fires it after Step 1 has parsed the plan; the cleanup-section header on line 187 remains "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene"; qwen reports no diff hunk places the trigger in Step 1 and cites `tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py:245-264`.
- requirement: A contract test must pin the issue-mode cleanup trigger's placement after Step 1 reads the plan and verify the cleanup header distinguishes issue-mode timing.
  expected_change_site: `tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py`
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: Google cites `tests/test_implement_plan_claude.py:245-264` as checking text existence without pinning trigger placement relative to Step 1, the header text, or an operational trigger at the end of Step 1; Minimax cites `tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py:245-264` as not asserting Step 1 references cleanup, header timing, or placement outside the strict step-0 invariant. Deepseek states `docs/INVENTORY.md:129` documents `scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py`, which differs from the inventory absence claims below.
- requirement: When Step 1 reads a plan that lacks a `Source issue:` header line, the issue-mode cleanup must either log/report the skip or be documented as an intentional no-op so an operator can tell whether the cleanup ran but matched nothing versus the resume being in project mode.
  expected_change_site: `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` and the workflow-templates twin, the new Step 0 bullet at line 12 and the cleanup-section "Issue mode: stopped stage sessions." bullet at line 190.
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The new bullet at line 12 says "a plan without that line skips this" but never instructs the session to log/report the skip; the cleanup-section report line at line 192 only fires when `m` is computable, so a project-mode resume with no `Source issue:` line never produces a count or log.
- requirement: The lint check (`tests/inventory_parity.py`) must pass; `scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py` must be documented in the `docs/INVENTORY.md` Scripts section or explicitly exempted in `tests/inventory_exemptions.txt`.

- `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md)` | `Line or code reference: 187` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The Zombie-checker cleanup header says "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene" but the issue-mode resume-without-block path at line 12 defers cleanup until after step 1 reads the plan (because the source issue identifier is only available then).
  WHY: Does not fail at runtime — the deferral bullet at line 12 explicitly overrides the timing. This is documentation imprecision, not a behavior defect.

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` | `Line or code reference: Step 0 bullet regarding Zombie-checker cleanup (line 12 in diff)` | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The cleanup trigger is placed within Step 0 (Preflight), but the instruction text requires the `Source issue:` identifier to run the label check, which is only resolved at Step 1 (Plan resolution).
  WHY: Step 0 executes before Step 1. Attempting cleanup at the end of Step 0 means the cleanup lack the necessary issue identifier, causing the label check to fail or be skipped, which re-introduces the bug of unarchived stopped sessions that this PR aims to fix.

  Evidence of absence: The PR diff does not update docs/INVENTORY.md to include scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py; tests/inventory_parity.py fails on this PR head, blocking the merge.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and byte-identical twin workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md)` | `Line or code reference: line 12 (new Step 0 child bullet), line 187 (Zombie-checker cleanup section header "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene"), line 190 (new "Issue mode: stopped stage sessions." bullet whose predicate reads \`Source issue:\` from the plan header)` | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The cleanup trigger for the issue-mode-without-`— resume.`-block path is delivered as a child of Step 0 (Session preflight), but the predicate it invokes (`mcp__github__issue_read get_labels` against the `<owner>/<repo>#<N>` parsed from the plan header's `Source issue:` line) requires data only available after Step 1's `Read` in full.
  WHY: After a `/reclarify` resume lands in `/implement-issue-claude` and hands off to `/implement-plan-claude`, the resuming session walks Step 0's bullets, hits the new issue-mode bullet, and either tries the cleanup (no source issue) or defers (no trigger). In both cases the stopped `— blocked on issue` session stays in the session list until a human archives it.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "When an issue-mode `/implement-plan-claude` project stops (`Status: BLOCKED`), the stage session that stopped stays open after a human answers on the issue and comments `/reclarify`. It then has to be archived by hand." The fix's contract is that the cleanup actually fires on `/reclarify` resume, after Step 1 reads the plan and the `Source issue:` identifier is available.
  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` (and byte-identical twin `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md`).
  Evidence of absence: No diff hunk places the issue-mode cleanup trigger inside Step 1 or appends an operational hook at the end of Step 1 to invoke the cleanup. The new Step 0 child bullet at line 12 (and the line-190 "Issue mode: stopped stage sessions." bullet it invokes) describe the cleanup but provide no runtime mechanism that fires it after Step 1 has parsed the plan. The cleanup-section header on line 187 is unchanged and still reads "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene, so stray checkers never pile up", without an exception for issue-mode timing. The diff is also missing a corresponding edit to the resume-hygiene section that would link Step 1's plan read to a deferred Step 0 action.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: A contract test must pin the issue-mode cleanup trigger's placement after Step 1 reads the plan and verify the cleanup section header distinguishes issue-mode timing, so a future edit cannot silently regress the trigger.
  Expected change site: `tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py` — extend `test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions` (or add a sibling test) to assert the cleanup-section header explicitly excludes issue mode from the "step 0" invariant, and that a Step 1 instruction (or equivalent operational hook) invokes the issue-mode cleanup after `Read` in full.
  Evidence of absence: The added test at `tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py:245-264` only checks text-string existence (the `blocked on issue` title, the bullet headers, the `Source issue:` header references, the failure-path strings, and a positive `blocked on issue` collision check). It does not assert that Step 1 has any reference to the cleanup, does not assert the cleanup-section header mentions issue-mode timing, and does not assert that the new Step 0 bullet is positioned outside the strict step-0-cleanup invariant. None of the other tests in `tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py` reference these strings either.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: When Step 1 reads a plan that lacks a `Source issue:` header line, the issue-mode cleanup must either log/report the skip or be documented as an intentional no-op so an operator can tell whether the cleanup ran but matched nothing versus the resume being in project mode.
  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` (and the workflow-templates twin), the new Step 0 bullet at line 12 and the cleanup-section "Issue mode: stopped stage sessions." bullet at line 190.
  Evidence of absence: The new bullet at line 12 says "a plan without that line skips this" but never instructs the session to log/report the skip (e.g. `stopped stage sessions kept: not in issue mode`).
